evidence.finding: The module documents that every scenario and timestamp produces three samples, one for each vehicle ego, with the infrastructure and the other vehicles as cooperators.
All agent YAML files are first grouped by the same scenario and timestamp.
The converter parses one shared agent_data collection for that physical event.
The converter loops over vehicle ego IDs, reuses the same event-level agent_data, changes the reference ego, and emits a separate sample index for every projection.
Ground truth is recomputed in each ego coordinate frame and the ego/cooperator roles differ, so the three rows are not byte-identical duplicates.

releasedMiniIndexEvidence.finding: All 180 physical events in the CRC-verified distributed mini indexes have four ego projections, including infrastructure agent 0. The distributed indexes therefore do not match the fixed converter's three-vehicle-ego contract.

interpretation: The projections are legitimate receiver-conditioned tasks and may add training value.
They share one physical traffic event, one timestamp, the same event-level sensor files, and the same underlying participants; they are therefore statistically clustered.
Counting projected rows as independent road acquisitions would overstate an independent-event count.

The fixed converter emits three vehicle-ego projections, while the distributed mini indexes contain four projections including infrastructure ego; this is a release-regeneration protocol mismatch, not proof of leakage or metric inflation.
Neither the static converter audit nor the mini index audit proves train-test leakage, metric inflation, or that multi-ego training lacks value.

mergedResearchCandidate.workingTitle: Release-regeneration parity and physical-event inference for multi-ego cooperative benchmarks
falsifiableHypotheses: Paired confidence intervals clustered by physical event are materially wider than intervals that resample projected ego rows independently for at least one close method comparison.

At a fixed number of unique physical-event exposures and optimizer steps, using all ego projections may still improve performance; if so, the gain is valid augmentation rather than evidence of additional independent events.
The fixed converter and the distributed index define materially different evaluation populations because only the latter includes infrastructure ego.

If release and regenerated protocols, cluster-aware and row-wise intervals, and method order are all practically equivalent, the release obtains a bounded protocol and statistical robustness certificate.
minimumStudy: Regenerate indexes with the fixed official converter and compare canonical release-versus-regenerated manifests before any model analysis.
Add a physical_event_id derived only from scenario and timestamp, plus a projection_id for ego identity and a protocol_id for released versus regenerated indexes.
Verify sensor-file overlap, role changes, infrastructure-ego inclusion, and annotations across all projected rows in the official train, validation, and test information files.
Cache paired per-event method outcomes for at least two fixed checkpoints or released predictions.
Compare vehicle-only, infrastructure-only, row-weighted, equal-event-weighted, and physical-event paired inference without treating projections as new acquisition units.
Run equal-physical-event training ablations with one random ego, cyclic ego, vehicle-only all-ego, and four-ego projections while matching optimizer steps and unique event exposure.
primaryMetrics: Intraclass correlation of paired per-row outcomes
successCriteria: Every released and regenerated row can be deterministically mapped to a physical event, projection, and protocol without collisions or missing provenance.
At least one result establishes either a reproducible inference change or a bounded equivalence certificate.
All statistical intervals preserve pairing by physical event and expose the 14-take continuous-campaign limitation separately.
killCriteria: Neither the released nor regenerated information files preserve stable physical-event provenance.
No fixed checkpoints, predictions, or feasible training baseline can support a paired outcome comparison.
A prior primary paper already publishes the same physical-event ledger, paired cluster analysis, and equal-exposure multi-ego ablation for CooperScene.

claimGuardrails: Do not call the projections duplicate acquisitions; use receiver-conditioned or counterfactual ego projections.
Do not call the design data leakage unless an event or underlying file crosses a declared train-test boundary.
Do not infer confidence-interval changes before paired outcomes are computed.
Do not treat any ego projections, their frames, or random resamples as independent acquisitions.
Do not infer which index protocol produced a published result without command, artifact, and checkpoint provenance.
Do not claim a population result from the 14 CooperScene takes, which belong to one finite continuous collection campaign.
